svg.text: A day in the life of an RDMA WRITE in NCCL, with the code
Same flow as the RDMA overview drawing. Each box adds, in purple, the main functions and structs that do its job (or, for hardware, set it up).
every GPU calls it; here GPU 0 sends one chunk to GPU 1
returns when every chunk has arrived and been added
puts the chunk in the send buffer (GPU memory), flags the proxy
launches the NCCL CUDA kernel on the GPU
adds the received chunk to its own, passes it on
the NCCL CUDA kernel waits for the proxy's flag,
then reduces the data in GPU memory
sees “write here” (CTS) from B, posts the RDMA WRITEs
net_ib/p2p.cc ncclIbIsend (reads the CTS from the FIFO)
sends CTS; later polls the CQ and flushes so the GPU sees the data
writes the WQEs, rings the doorbell, polls the CQ
posts RECV WQEs, polls the CQ
reads the WQE, then reads the data straight from GPU memory
QP set up by: mlx5_ib_create_qp → CREATE_QP
checks the rkey, writes straight into GPU memory, writes a CQE
rkey checked against the MKEY made by
cuts into packets, numbers them (PSN), waits for ACK, resends
checks the QP and packet order (PSN), sends ACK
receives the packets, strips the headers
same port settings on both sides
CTS: “write here”, a small RDMA WRITE sent by B's libmlx5 and NIC
code that does or sets up the box
Files: NCCL src/ and src/transport/net_ib/; rdma-core providers/mlx5/; kernel drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx5/. Indented lines are called from the line above (some steps in between are skipped).
Checked against NCCL master, rdma-core master and Linux master, November 2026. QP = queue pair. WQE = work queue entry. CQE = completion queue entry. MKEY = the NIC's memory key (lkey / rkey).
